description:
The measurement harness derives its backend schedule from the prototype crate's candidate registry through one stream-aware adapter, so the study has exactly one candidate list.

## Background

The harness and the prototype crate must not end up with two hand-maintained candidate lists that drift apart. The prototype crate carries the study's candidate registry; this work adds the adapter that derives the harness's `Backend::ALL` schedule from that registry, so a candidate registered once in the prototype crate becomes schedulable by the harness without a second list to update. Drift between two lists is silent until a cell is missing from a receipt, which is why the equality of the two sets is asserted by a test rather than by review.

The adapter is also where a candidate's stream purpose is bound, so a scheduled path draws from the purpose domain the harness assigned it rather than from one chosen at the call site.

A path registered through the adapter is scheduled by both the equivalence check and the timing grid and cannot silently miss a cell; a path whose implementation has not landed reports itself unsupported with a stated reason, which is how the harness already records a backend it cannot run.

This leaf follows the timing-column leaf on a dependency edge because the two rework the same harness files; the ordering keeps every footprint overlap on an edge and costs no wave, since this leaf's wave siblings are the field candidate leaves.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The harness derives its backend schedule from the prototype crate's candidate registry through one adapter, so a candidate registered once in that registry is schedulable without a second hand-maintained list in the harness.
- [hard] REQ-02: A candidate reached through that adapter draws from the stream purpose domain the harness assigned it, with no numeric stream base computed at the call site.
- [hard] REQ-03: A registered candidate whose implementation has not landed is reported as unsupported with a stated reason rather than omitted from the schedule.
- [hard] REQ-04: A test asserts that the set of paths the harness schedules equals the set the prototype registry enumerates, so a candidate cannot exist in one and be missing from the other.
- [hard] REQ-05: `cargo test --manifest-path dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/Cargo.toml --release` passes.

## Notes

Scope is the schedule adapter alone. The per-phase timing columns land before this leaf on its dependency edge, and no campaign receipt is produced here.

Every crate under `dev/research/` is excluded from the default Cargo workspace, so the workspace CI pipeline never compiles them; the explicit `--manifest-path` invocation above is the only build evidence for this change.
title: Registry-derived schedule adapter for prototype candidates
